attributes.board_name: Iowa Board of Speech Pathology and Audiology (Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing)

rules.accepted_credit_types: Programs offered by AAA or ASHA, or offered/approved in advance by national, state or local SLP/audiology associations, schools of SLP/audiology, or universities and colleges; in-person, journal reading, teleconference, videoconference and online (home study needs a passed posttest); presenting new material 2 h per hour, max 16; academic courses (1 semester hour = 15 h); government regulations, CPR, child/dependent adult abuse and business topics combined max 6 h (business max 2); passing the Praxis exam may replace CE
rules.new_licensee_rule: No CE required for the first renewal; CE earned from initial licensure until the second renewal may be used. A license issued within six months of the renewal date is not renewed until the following renewal date.
rules.carryover: Up to 50% of the required hours (max 13) may be carried to the next renewal period.
rules.audit_note: The board selects licensees for audit; keep proof of attendance (date, location, title, presenter, contact hours, certificate). Keep mandatory reporter training documentation for three years.

topics.who: Licensees who examine, attend, counsel or treat children and/or dependent adults: the applicable Iowa HHS training on identifying and reporting child and/or dependent adult abuse (481 IAC 740.9(4)); hours not set in the board rule

rules.notes: One hour = at least 50 minutes. The compliance period runs January 1 of an even year to December 31 of the next odd year; CE must be completed before submitting the renewal. A person holding both SLP and audiology licenses must meet the 26 hours for each profession. Iowa does not license SLP or audiology assistants (unlicensed, supervised under 481 IAC 740.8).
rules.rule_quote: Each biennium, a person who is licensed to practice as a speech pathology or audiology licensee in this state will be required to complete a minimum of 26 hours of continuing education approved by the board.
